Photograph scan of an original photo of a tree-planting ceremony on the Buckham Memorial Library grounds in 1932. 13 women of the Nature Study Club, standing around the hole, shovel still in the ground, women in overcoats. Back of print has information about the persons in the photo.  "Notes by Edgar W. Pye, grandson of Mrs. E.H. Loyhed & Mrs Mills Pye."
notes: Katy Pye sent a typed letter to Susan Garwood which has additional information about the club: "I had an interesting conversation with my  Uncle, Edgar Pye, .... about the Nature Study Club's room in the Library. He said a small portion of the second floor reading room (separated by an 8 step walk-up) was dedicated to the Club. It contained nature books, a display of arrow heads, and framed mountings of North and South American butterflies. My great Uncle, Donald Loyhed, was working for a mining Company in South America and sent two sets of  Butterflies to his mother, Mrs. Edgar Lyhed. She had them framed and gave them to the Nature Study Club room where they hung for many years. Mrs. Grant gave the set of North American species and Mrs. Sheffield provided lovely furniture. Veseli was incorporated as a village in an election held April 23, 1889. As an individual political center, it had its own waterworks, town hall and fire department. Deforest Albert Skinner was born July 15, 1869 in New York, married Nettie B. Cowder in New York on October 18, 1893 and had 3 children. He died in Faribault in August 1928. He was a grocer in Minneapolis in 1880, and he ran a creamery and ice cream business in Faribault in 1900-1920. He also served in indian wars in 1888 and 1889, including a battle near the scene of General Custer's last stand. He opened a harness and saddlery shop in St. Paul, which he ran from 1892-1893.

Dear Sir - 

It occures to me that you might enjoy seeing this photo of a mail wagon owned by my father and I used on rout 4 up to 1915.  My father was Harry B. McIlvaine, and the team was "Jerry, the Cherry Picker" and Bill McKinley, the bay horse.

Historic Walking tour-  1  1st St. SW  E.K. Clements House built in 1892,  He was a dentist for 68 years.  He married Mary Wheeler.  Buckham bought the house in 1901.  Mrs. Buckham built the library across from the house in 1929-30 to honor Mr. Buckham.  Queen Ann  Style Architecture with Bay window where the door is now, shell above the 3rd floor is Classical Style.  Taken in 2001,  3" by 5" B&W photo

Historic Walking tour-  115  1st Ave. SW.,  F.A. Theopold Sr's House, built in 1874-1875, The lighter colored brick resembles Milwaukee brick.  The brick was made at Carver.  Italianate style.  The house is contemporary with the Hill House, Cole House, & Hudson Wilson House.  All were built around the same time.  Theopold Sr. built Depot Square & had a grocery business there with a candy business at the east end of the building.  Located in the house later were the Assembly of God Church, K.C. Hall (one year), apartment housing, and in 2001 a private residence.  Taken in 2001,  3" by 5" B&W photo

caption: 148 - Peterka family
credit: Copies from Mr. Smith's private collection.
descrip:
Peterka Family: Rose, Joe, Ann, Frank, Elizabeth, Antonia, Mary, Steve, Father Voclav, Katie, Mother Mary
This picture was taken soon after the Peterka family arrived in St. Paul from Czechoslovakia. Betty was three years old when they left Europe. Everybody in the family was seasick. The Peterka family was sponsored by an aunt, Mrs. Jirovec, who worked with the priest in the Bohemian parish in St. Paul. They purchased tickets for their journey and helped them get settled and find jobs. The three oldest girls worked in a cigar factory to help support the family. Mary, the oldest in the family, married Vaclov Landa in October, 1908. They moved to Lonsdale in 1915. Vaclov passed away in 1938. Marry will be 96 in October.

Copy of a photo of Phelps Cottge at Shattuck School.  According to the donor:
"The original was a Library for Seabury Divinity School and later converted into a dormitory.  The building was financed by a bequest from Lucy Phelps of Winsted, CT.  The western part of the building was erected in the summer of 1869 as the library for the Divinity School, after Seabury moved to its new campus the buildig was sold to Shattuck School and a small stonewing facing east was added.  Renamed Phelps Cottage it served as a dormitory for 15 boys until into the 1920s.
